Thanks Neha — quick tech notes from my side (posting here so Ghostship has visibility):

1) Integration model options
   - Direct API embed: Ghostship calls Redwood hosted endpoints (fastest to market). Requires token routing and per-tenant keys.
   - Dedicated partner pool: reserved capacity for Ghostship tenants (better latency / isolation). Requires minimum commit.
   - On-prem: packaging + installation playbook for air-gapped installs (longer lead, higher TCO).

2) Telemetry & data considerations
   - We can provide per-tenant telemetry and token-level cost breakdowns, but customers must opt-in to sharing runtime logs for debugging.
   - PII redaction policy: by default Redwood does not persist full requests beyond 24 hours for hosted; for Private we can follow partner retention SLA.

3) Support & SLA tiers
   - Standard: email + dev portal, 48–72h P1 response
   - Premier (partner): 8x5 phone + 4h P1 response, 99.5% availability SLA for dedicated pools

4) Security checklist items (for legal/security review)
   - SOC 2 Type II report, incoming/outgoing data flow diagrams, SSO/SAML config docs, KMS integration options

I'll add a short section to the checklist on recommended commit sizes for a dedicated pool and expected lead times.

— Karthik

1) Commercial: prefer a hybrid model — 70/30 rev share (Ghostship/Redwood) for embeds in multi-tenant SaaS customers and a fixed per-instance license for on-prem deployments. Can you provide a worked example (3-year term) with estimated ARR impact?

2) Support: require a named escalation path and a 2-hour P1 response for high-severity security incidents during onboarding windows (first 90 days). Can Redwood commit to a limited temporary SLA for onboarding?

Also attaching a short Ghostship checklist with their compliance must-haves.

Ben / Alice — appreciated the clear asks and the checklist. Quick replies and attachments below.

1) Commercial worked example: attached a 3-year worked example that models both hybrid rev-share (70/30) and fixed-instance license for on-prem. High level: with a mid-size rollout (10k MAUs, 1.2B tokens/mo) the hybrid rev-share yields ~ $2.1M ARR to Ghostship in year 2 vs. fixed-license of $1.4M (numbers in attached SOW PDF). We included assumptions on token mix and cost-of-serving.

2) Temporary onboarding SLA: Redwood can offer a 90-day onboarding SLA with a 2-hour P1 response window for security incidents during deployment windows, provided Ghostship purchases Premier partner support for the onboarding period (add-on one-time fee to cover 24/7 incident pager). We'll codify this in the SOW.

3) Operational handoff: proposed runbook — 2-week technical onboarding, shared test environment, monthly ops sync for first 6 months, and access to per-tenant telemetry dashboards.

Next steps:
- Ghostship to confirm preferred commercial model by 12/08
- If confirmed, Redwood legal will circulate a redline-ready SOW and an MSA addendum for OEM embed in 48–72 hours
- Schedule a technical kickoff week of 12/06

I'm attaching: Redwood_OEM_Draft_SOW_20261201.pdf (contains worked financial example) and a cleaned OEM checklist that includes technical lead times.

Best,
